subject: physics_2
question_text: If a wire is stretched to double its original length without loss of mass, how will the resistivity of the wire be influenced?

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Transcription: the book (p28, VSAQ 22) puts a space before the question mark; it is dropped. The second mark is invented and rewards the contrast with resistance, which the book does not print — the book answers only 'it remains same, because it depends on nature of the material'. Hand-checked: resistivity is a material property and does not change; with the mass fixed the volume Al is fixed, so doubling l halves A and R = ρl/A becomes 4R.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The resistivity is unchanged
lines: Resistivity ρ is a property of the material
itself. Stretching changes the shape of the
wire, not the material it is made of.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Answer the question asked: the resistivity stays the same.
steps.why: Resistivity is fixed by the material and its temperature — how many free electrons it has and how often they collide. Pulling a wire longer does not change either of those, so ρ is unchanged.
common_mistakes: Saying the resistivity becomes 4 times. That is the resistance, not the resistivity.
Saying it halves because the wire is thinner.

recall.must_convey: That the resistivity stays the same because it is a property of the material, not of the shape.
accept: it depends only on the material

steps.memory_tip: Resistivity belongs to the material; resistance belongs to the piece of wire.

steps.label: What does change
lines: The resistance does change. The mass is the
same, so the volume Al is the same: doubling
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Separate the two clearly: ρ fixed, R four times.
steps.why: Constant mass and constant density mean constant volume, so length times area is fixed. Length up by 2 and area down by 2 both push the resistance up, and 2 × 2 gives the factor 4.
common_mistakes: Doubling the resistance only. The area halves as well, so the factor is 4, not 2.
Forgetting that constant mass fixes the volume.

recall.must_convey: That constant volume halves the area when the length doubles, so the resistance becomes four times.

steps.memory_tip: Twice as long and half as thick: 2 × 2 = 4.

insider_note: The question asks about resistivity, and the common slip is to answer with the resistance. Write the resistivity answer first, then the resistance as a separate line.
